title: Poland's per-capita CO₂ emissions are more than double Sweden's, despite both being EU member states.
source: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025, via Our World in Data · 2023 data
caveat: Territorial emissions: excludes emissions embedded in imported goods and international aviation.
subject: POL
alt: Map of Europe. All 41 countries in the study set are shaded by their 2023 per-capita CO2 emissions, from a light shade under 2 tonnes to a dark shade at 10 tonnes and above; the frame cuts through 5 of them (Finland, Norway, Portugal, Sweden, Ukraine), which are shaded but not wholly visible. Poland, outlined and named, is in the 6-to-8-tonne class at 7.3 tonnes per person — more than double Sweden's 3.5 tonnes. Sweden is the comparison, not the minimum: it is 5th lightest of 41, and the lightest shading on the map belongs to Albania at 1.6 tonnes.
